- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to align with mean-reversion bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >10%), model overcorrects in next period; apply downward bias of 3–8% to prevent overshoot.  
- If true price deviates from 30-day moving average by >5%, model is lagging; adjust forecast to closer to recent 7-day average.  
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 5 days, model fails to adjust; apply a 1–3% correction in direction of sentiment shift.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is >15% above model, assume sentiment-driven overconfidence; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 7-day horizon.
